title: On Wicked: For Good @Joe Weinberg #broadway #musicaltheatre #film #ra...
transcript: I'm gonna rank every movie musical adapted from the stage that's been released since 2020 I'm sure we're gonna disagree feel free to tell me how wrong I am in the comments but please keep it classy and remember the stakes couldn't be lower! in last place I have Dear Evan Hansen and you know we talk a lot about how he looked too old for the role we don't talk enough about how appallingly Razzie-level bad he was my kinda hot take is I actually find this story kind of compelling in a twisted sort of way but his performance drags it down kicking and screaming next I have 13 and you know the original is obviously aimed at younger audiences but this movie feels genuinely kiddie like I felt too old to be watching it partly because I think the adaptation and direction remove some of the bite from it. I think the heartwarming side of The Prom works fairly well but the satirical, social commentary side I think is so poorly done in both the musical and the film. I actually think it works slightly better in the context of film than in the echo chamber of Broadway but still, not for me! next I have Cyrano based on the 2019 off-Broadway musical I have a soft spot for this story Peter Dinklage is great and I like a lot of the music but most of the lyrics are pretty bad and for a story that's literally about beautiful poetry that's a big problem and overall the vision for this adaptation felt kind of flat and awkward I don't hate the Mean Girls movie musical as much as most people do I actually think it works somewhat better than on stage but still I don't think the addition of songs to this story brings enough to the table to ever make me wanna watch this over the original with The Color Purple I think the performances combined with Alice Walker's beautiful story and emotionally rich themes still serve as a solid foundation for this film. but the additions to the score make the screenplay feel extremely cramped and rushed and with the dreamalike presentation of the musical numbers I get what they were going for but I think it undermined the storytelling more than anything. next up D!cks: the musical based on the 2014 off-Broadway show F*cking Identical Twins I really respect the swing for the fences here like I'm so impressed they even got this movie made and I enjoyed the first half well enough, but the second half got a little too grotesque and off the rails for my taste personally. I've actually never seen Everybody's Talking About Jamie on stage this film is my only touchpoint it's hyper sentimental, maybe a bit too saccharine but there's enough charm and heart here that I think they mostly got away with it. with Kiss of the Spider Woman The story, the performances, the concept, and the score are doing a lot of heavy lifting to make this a pretty engaging watch but as a film adaptation I was a little underwhelmed they were going for this old Hollywood sound stage aesthetic that sometimes came across more like cheap, made-for-TV movie and while I understand the choice to cut all the non-diegetic songs I thought it was a little cowardly. in 6th place I have the newest edition, Wicked: For Good which I did a video about that I'll link in the caption it's definitely flawed but for me it still made for a compelling and emotionally satisfying payoff for this epic take on the Wicked story. and shockingly coming in 5th place, Wicked part 1. it's definitely better than part 2 because of the material they have to work with but overall I think these movies share a lot of the same strengths and weaknesses and in general for me they do a great job bringing the spirit of the stage musical to the screen in 4th place: Tick, Tick…Boom! Andrew Garfield is incredible and I think it's a cleverly conceived adaptation in how it blends biography with autobiography I do think they go a little overboard with the cameos and Easter eggs though I found it kind of distracting in 3rd place: I've never loved the original book of West Side Story so I really appreciated Tony Kushner's new take on it (for the most part at least) and the score is as beautiful as ever. in 2nd place — hear me out I admit this movie is very flawed you don't have to tell me but for all the clunky additions and unfortunate cuts In the Heights is one of my favorite musicals of all time and the film gives me the same warm, vibrant, heart-wrenching feeling that the stage show does and of all the movies on this list it's by far the one I've rewatched the most but in 1st place let's not forget the Matilda movie musical adaptation, which honestly still slaps it's beautifully done and in some ways it even improves on the stage musical which is already one of my other all-time favorites
